subject: Maths
title: Maths Exam 7
intro: Edexcel Higher style. No calculator. Type powers with ^ (for example x^2). Show your working: method marks count even if the final answer slips.

questions.ms: 15x⁵. Multiply the numbers, add the powers.
x² + 2x − 24. M1 all four terms x² − 4x + 6x − 24, A1.
5x(3x − 2). B1 for a partial factorisation such as 5(3x² − 2x) or x(15x − 10).

questions.q: Make t the subject of the formula s = (u + v)t2
questions.ms: t = 2s/(u + v). M1 2s = (u + v)t, A1 divide by (u + v).

questions.q:
Here are the first four terms of an arithmetic sequence.
7, 11, 15, 19, …
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term.
Is 100 a term in the sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, …? You must give a reason.
questions.ms: No. M1 4n + 3 = 100 so n = 24.25 (or terms 99 and 103 found), A1 not a whole number so 100 is not a term.

questions.q: The nth term of a sequence is 2n2 + 1. Work out the 5th term.
questions.ms: 51. 2 × 5² + 1 = 2 × 25 + 1 (square first, then × 2).
x = 4, y = 2. M1 add to eliminate y: 4x = 16, M1 substitute, A1 both.

questions.q:
2 pens and 3 rulers cost £3.30
4 pens and 1 ruler cost £3.10
Work out the cost of one pen. Give your answer in pence.
questions.ms: 60p. M1 2p + 3r = 330 and 4p + r = 310, M1 eliminate one letter (e.g. ×2 first equation: 4p + 6r = 660, subtract: 5r = 350), M1 r = 70, A1 p = 60.

questions.q: Which is the best estimate of 8.1 × 0.490.0198?
questions.ms: 200. 8 × 0.5 = 4, and 4 ÷ 0.02 = 200. Dividing by a small decimal makes the answer much bigger.

questions.q:
360 = 23 × 32 × 5
Write 3602 as a product of its prime factors in index form.
questions.ms: 2⁶ × 3⁴ × 5². Squaring doubles each power. B1 for two powers correct.

questions.q:
A square has an area of 45 cm2.
Work out the perimeter of the square. Give your answer in the form a√5
Show that 3(x + 5) − 2(x + 1) ≡ x + 13 and explain why this is an identity.
questions.ms: M1 3x + 15 − 2x − 2, A1 = x + 13, B1 true for every value of x (both sides are always equal), so it is an identity.
